reconstructed_theorem_text: For every finite-dimensional real inner-product normed vector space E equipped with its Borel measurable structure and every polynomial p with real coefficients, let S={w:E | norm(w)=1} carry the subspace topology and induced Borel structure inherited from E, and let gamma=stdGaussian(E), the actual centered identity-covariance standard Gaussian on E. Write f_w(x)=p.eval(inner_product(w,x)). There exists a single family hfeature witnessing MemLp(f_w,2,gamma) for every w in S. For this family define F(w)=(hfeature(w)).toLp(f_w), an element of the actual real L2(gamma) quotient space. Then F:S->L2(gamma) is continuous in its L2 norm topology, and the following assertions hold for every measure rho on S which is a probability measure. First, for every x in E, the scalar function w->p.eval(inner_product(w,x)) is genuinely Bochner integrable under rho. Second, F is genuinely Bochner integrable under rho with values in L2(gamma). Third, for the fixed pointwise actual scalar mean M_rho(x)=integral_S p.eval(inner_product(w,x)) drho(w), there exists hmean witnessing MemLp(M_rho,2,gamma) such that (hmean).toLp(M_rho)=integral_S F(w) drho(w), as an equality in L2(gamma). The left-side integral defining M_rho is real-valued, and its integrability is certified for every x, not just gamma-almost every x. The right-side integral is a vector Bochner integral in L2(gamma), and its integrability is separately concluded. Both integrals run over the whole parameter space S under rho; gamma is the data-space Gaussian used for L2 membership and equivalence, not the integrating measure in these parameter integrals. All ridge memberships, continuity, scalar and vector integrability, averaged-function L2 membership, and the exact quotient-space identity are conclusions. The only law-dependent premise is that the universally considered rho has total mass one. The same hfeature and F are fixed before rho is quantified, while hmean may depend on rho and proves membership of the already specified actual scalar mean rather than choosing a different function. The identity is in L2 equivalence classes; any selected representative of the vector integral agrees with the raw scalar mean only gamma-almost everywhere, with no pointwise equality of chosen representatives asserted. The parameter probability may be arbitrary, including nonatomic laws; no finite-support restriction appears. No positive dimension or nonzero-polynomial premise is imposed. If E is zero dimensional then S is empty, the feature family and continuity are vacuous, and the probability-law implication has no rho satisfying its premise. For p=0 all displayed feature and mean functions and quotient values are zero.
objects: E with its finite-dimensional real inner-product normed and Borel measurable structures; real polynomial p; unit-parameter subspace S; fixed standard Gaussian gamma on E; raw scalar ridge functions f_w; a single L2-membership proof family hfeature; the actual L2-class map F; arbitrary probability rho on S; actual pointwise scalar parameter mean M_rho; its L2 proof hmean; and the vector Bochner integral of F under rho.
domains: E has NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace R, FiniteDimensional R, MeasurableSpace, and BorelSpace structures. S={w:E | norm(w)=1} has the inherited norm subspace topology and Borel structure. p:Polynomial R is a finite real polynomial. Each f_w:E->R is measured in Lp R 2 gamma for gamma=stdGaussian(E). F maps S into that L2 quotient with its norm topology. rho:Measure S is arbitrary subject to IsProbabilityMeasure rho. The scalar parameter integrals map each x:E to R; the vector integral has target Lp R 2 gamma. No positive dimension is assumed; completeness of E follows from finite dimensionality over R.
quantifiers: For every E with the displayed structures and every p, there exists one family hfeature:forall w:S, MemLp(f_w,2,gamma). In the scope of that witness, F is continuous and for every rho:Measure S, if rho is a probability then: for every x:E the scalar parameter section is integrable; F is vector-Bochner integrable; and there exists hmean:MemLp(M_rho,2,gamma) giving the exact class equality with the vector integral. The existential hfeature precedes the universal rho quantifier, so one family works for all probability laws. The existential hmean is inside the probability-law scope and may depend on rho. Neither witness chooses a different raw function.
assumptions: Only the displayed finite-dimensional real inner-product and Borel measurable structures and a given arbitrary real polynomial p. The universally quantified parameter law must have mass one. Feature L2 membership, continuity of F, scalar parameter integrability, vector parameter integrability, and L2 membership of the actual scalar average are all generated conclusions, not supplied hypotheses. No finite-support, density, extra parameter-law regularity, nonzero polynomial, or positive-dimensionality condition appears.
conclusion: There is one family proving genuine Gaussian L2 membership of all exact unit-weight polynomial ridges, and its actual class map F is continuous. For every probability rho on S, each raw scalar parameter section w->p.eval(inner_product(w,x)) is genuinely integrable for every x:E, F is genuinely integrable as an L2(gamma)-valued function, and the actual scalar mean M_rho is in L2(gamma). Its actual quotient class equals exactly the L2-valued Bochner parameter integral: toLp(M_rho)=integral_S F drho. No estimate factor or unidentified alternative mean is used.
scopes: The Gaussian gamma lives on the data space E and governs every L2 membership, norm topology, and almost-everywhere equivalence. Parameter integrals are over S under rho. Scalar integrability is pointwise in every x and yields a genuine real integral at each x. Vector integrability is a separate conclusion, certifying almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite integral of the L2 norm under rho. The resulting mean membership certifies gamma-almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite L2 seminorm in x. The final equality is in the quotient L2 space; it does not require pointwise equality of arbitrary selected representatives with the raw mean. The map F and hfeature are fixed uniformly over rho. Arbitrary probability laws, including nonatomic ones, are covered. With empty S in zero dimension, the membership/continuity assertions are vacuous and there is no probability measure satisfying the later premise. The statement supplies actual integrability, so the asserted integrals do not rely on the totalized values of nonintegrable Bochner expressions.
constant_dependencies: There is no named norm bound, explicit continuity modulus, averaging denominator, or numerical estimate constant. The exact identity has coefficient 1. Dependence is on the fixed E,p,gamma, and the chosen probability rho for M_rho and its integral; the feature map itself is independent of rho. Probability mass one is the only supplied scalar normalization of the parameter law. No finite-particle count or norm-dependent budget occurs.
